pros: Easy to understand and interpret (percentage of shared neighbors)
Accounts for both common and total neighbors simultaneously
Simple and computationally efficient set operations
No parameters to tune or optimize
Symmetric and well-defined for all node pairs
Natural distance metric when converted (1 - Jaccard)
Robust baseline for comparing complex link prediction algorithms
Widely applicable beyond graphs (sets, documents, biology)
Handles varying node degrees through automatic normalization
cons: Does not consider neighbor importance or weighted connections
Penalizes high-degree nodes more than Sørensen-Dice
Cannot capture structural patterns beyond immediate neighbors
Zero score when nodes share no common neighbors (limited coverage)
Sensitive to noise and missing edges in sparse graphs
May underestimate similarity in dense network regions
Equal treatment of all neighbors ignores connection strength
Not suitable for directed graphs without modification
Biased towards lower scores in scale-free networks
Less effective for very large graphs where most pairs have score 0
